name: Chronic Fatigue Syndrome

criteria.description: Substantial reduction in ability to engage in pre-illness levels of activity for > 6 months, accompanied by fatigue that is profound, of new onset, not result of ongoing exertion, and not substantially relieved by rest
Post-exertional malaise (PEM): worsening of symptoms after physical, cognitive, or emotional exertion that would not have caused problems before illness
Cognitive impairment (problems with memory, concentration, information processing)
Orthostatic intolerance (symptoms worsened by upright posture, improved by lying down)

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: All 3 major criteria required, plus at least one of cognitive impairment OR orthostatic intolerance. Symptoms must be present at least half the time with moderate/severe intensity. Duration > 6 months.
diagnosticCriteria.notes: NICE 2021 lowered the duration threshold to 3 months for suspected diagnosis. PEM is considered the hallmark feature. Other conditions must be excluded.

pathognomonic.notes: Hallmark symptom; disproportionate worsening after minimal exertion, delayed onset 12-72 hours, prolonged recovery

common.symptomName: Profound fatigue not relieved by rest
searchTerms: extreme tiredness not helped by rest

common.notes: Slowed processing, difficulty concentrating, word-finding problems

rare.notes: Approximately 25% of patients are housebound or bedbound at some point

searchTerms: discomfort from bright lights and sounds

laboratory: No specific diagnostic biomarker currently validated
Routine labs (CBC, CMP, TSH, CRP/ESR) typically normal - used to exclude other conditions
Screen for celiac disease, adrenal insufficiency, HIV, hepatitis if clinically indicated
Research biomarkers: impaired natural killer cell function, cytokine abnormalities
imaging: Brain MRI: usually normal; may show nonspecific white matter lesions in some patients
genetic: Genome-wide association studies suggest multiple susceptibility loci
other: Tilt table test: may demonstrate orthostatic intolerance, NMH, or POTS
Cardiopulmonary exercise testing (2-day): reduced VO2 max on day 2 supports PEM
NASA Lean Test as office-based orthostatic challenge
Sleep study to exclude primary sleep disorders

distinguishingFeatures: Fibromyalgia has widespread pain as primary symptom with tender points
Fibromyalgia may have less prominent PEM
Hypothyroidism confirmed by elevated TSH and low free T4
POTS defined by HR increase >= 30 bpm on standing

redFlags: Focal neurological signs (investigate for MS, brain tumor)
Significant weight loss (exclude malignancy, adrenal insufficiency)
Lymphadenopathy that is progressive or persistently enlarged
references: Institute of Medicine. Beyond Myalgic Encephalomyelitis/Chronic Fatigue Syndrome: Redefining an Illness. National Academies Press. 2015.
National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE). Myalgic encephalomyelitis (or encephalopathy)/chronic fatigue syndrome: diagnosis and management. NICE Guideline NG206. 2021.
Bateman L, et al. Myalgic Encephalomyelitis/Chronic Fatigue Syndrome: Essentials of Diagnosis and Management. Mayo Clin Proc. 2021;96(11):2861-2878.
